builder-criteria.why: all 7 lines quoted in the builder brief

words-only.why: I compared each verifier check's PASS and FAIL conditions with the words of its expect line. Checks 1–5 test only for the exact stdout plus one trailing newline, and Check 1 also tests the exit 0 its line names. Using `od -c` is how the output gets checked, not an extra condition. Check 5 reads `\t` as the JSON escape, which matches the line and its proof. Check 6 requires `npm test` to exit 0 and at least one test that runs bin/csv2json.js with `--tsv` on input containing tabs and asserts on the output. Excluding tests that only call parse() follows from "runs bin/csv2json.js... checks its output". Check 7 requires only that `--tsv` is mentioned with an example invocation. The stricter items (`npm run test:cli`, whether the README says "tab-separated", flag placement, CRLF input, parse.js changes) all sit under Advisory. The criterion holds.

runs-as-written.why: I checked every command in both briefs. Builder: the `printf '…' | node bin/csv2json.js [--tsv]` pipelines, `; echo "exit=$?"` and `npm test` are all valid. bin/csv2json.js exists, and package.json has a `test` script (`node --test`). The JS snippets (`process.argv.slice(2)`, `parse(text, '\t')`, `execFileSync(...)`) are valid. The expected string `[{"a\\tb":"1\\t2"}]\n` is correct JS-literal notation for the JSON tab escape. Verifier: `node --version`, the pipes into `od -c`, `npm test; echo "exit=$?"` and `grep -rn -- '--tsv' test/` would all run as written, and the `--` stops grep from reading `--tsv` as an option. The issue's proof uses `npm run test:cli`, a script that doesn't exist. The verifier brief catches this: it only runs that script "If the PR adds one" and says its absence is not a failure. No step relies on a missing file or script, and no argument or syntax is wrong.

catches-traps.why: I checked both must_catch items. Item 1 holds: the builder brief's current-state section says test/csv.test.js has "a `parse` test and a `cli` test". Step 2 then says "Keep the existing tests passing". Step 1 says to call "`parse(text)` exactly as now" without the flag, and "Do not change src/parse.js unless you have to". Step 4 re-runs the CSV command and `npm test`. Together these name the CSV tests as something that must keep passing and protect the shared parse path. Item 2 holds: verifier Check 6 runs "`npm test; echo "exit=$?"`" instead of proof 6's script. The advisory section says "package.json has no such script" for `npm run test:cli`, and that its absence is not a failure. Both traps are handled.

avoids-must-not.why:
The briefs avoid both must_not items.

Item 1: the verifier's Check 6 bases PASS or FAIL on `npm test; echo "exit=$?"` and the grep of test/. `npm run test:cli` shows up only under "Advisory (does not change any PASS or FAIL above)", which also says "Its absence is not a failure." So no check depends on it.

Item 2: the builder brief brings up a general option only to rule it out: "Do not add quoting rules, separator auto-detection, a general --sep/--delimiter option, --help..." It asks only for a `--tsv` check that calls `parse(text, '\t')`.

The verifier's optional probes (flag position, CRLF input) are marked outside the acceptance lines and don't ask for any option the issue's non-goals rule out.

methods-private.why: The criterion is met. Nothing in the builder brief exists only in the verifier brief. Its step 4 commands are the issue's proof commands, such as `printf 'a\tb\n1\t2\n' | node bin/csv2json.js --tsv; echo "exit=$?"`, and the criterion allows those. The input/output pairs in step 2 copy the issue's expect lines 1, 2, 3 and 5, which the builder may see. It also tells the builder to write its own tests, which is allowed. The builder brief leaves out every verifier-only method: no `od -c` or `cmp` byte checks, no `grep -rn -- '--tsv' test/`, no `node --version`, and none of the advisory probes (`foo --tsv`, CRLF input, the `npm run test:cli` note). It has no PASS/FAIL wording either, such as "A test that only calls parse() directly… does not count." Its scope limits ("Do not add quoting rules…") restate the issue's non-goals, not the verifier's checks.
